Tom — thanks for the clear summary and for surfacing those asks. Short answers up front, then a proposed bakeoff scope attached.

Answers:
- Token cost: based on the demo model footprint we discussed, hosted API (standard quantized variant) is ~0.9x the token cost of your current provider for embeddings and ~1.1x for generation; dedicated/private quantized on-prem can reduce generation unit cost by ~30–45% depending on int8 vs int4 quantization and sequence length. I put a worked example in the attached CSV.
- Load test: yes — we can coordinate a 30-minute 2k QPS synthetic run against a sandbox cluster. We'll also capture cold-start behavior by cycling instances.
- Telemetry: Redwood Console will provide per-route token breakdowns (inference vs prompt), cache hit/miss rates, p95 latency traces, and a downloadable token-cost CSV per request ID. SOC logs (audit trail) are available for private deployments and can be exported to your S3/KMS.

Proposed bakeoff (attached: poa-bakeoff-matrix.csv) — summary:
- Objectives: throughput validation, p95 latency under load, correctness parity on 500 eval prompts, security evidence (KMS + audit export).
- Tests: 30-min 2k QPS synthetic; 1hr 500-prompt accuracy sweep; 2x failover cycles to test graceful routing.
- Success criteria: p95 < 120ms for chat gen (single-turn), embedding recall within 3% of baseline, KV cache hit rate > 60% for targeted prefix workload.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Security kickoff (Monica) — share SOC checklist + SSO/KMS details (Monica will own).
2) Procurement thread to set MSA terms (Jonas will initiate).
3) Bakeoff schedule — target week of Sep 14 for sandbox validation; we can shift earlier if needed.

I'll follow up with calendar invites and the sandbox endpoint.

Best,
